online_store_on.title: Turn on your online store
online_store_on.summary: Your online store is a public shop page with a cart and checkout. It needs a short setup, then one Publish click.

steps.text: Make sure the Online Store module is on. Open the System Builder, find "Online Store" and switch it on (it needs the Products module).
Open Online Store from the sidebar.

Open Settings and fill in: public business name, country and city, address, contact phone, pickup and/or delivery, a payment option that matches (pay at pickup, cash on delivery or bank transfer — bank transfer needs your bank details), and the warehouse that fulfils online orders.
Open Products and choose what customers can see: tick products and press Publish. At least one published product is required.
Go back to Overview and press "Publish store". If something is missing, the page lists exactly what.

steps: Share your store link or QR code from Overview — your first orders land in Orders, where you accept, prepare and complete them.
tips: You can pause new orders without hiding the store (the pause switch on Overview).
Your VenQore subscription must be active to publish.
Offers and coupon codes are under Offers in the same area.

online_orders_manage.title: Handle online orders
online_orders_manage.summary: Every online order lands in the Orders inbox with a countdown to accept it.

steps.text: Open Orders.

steps: Open an order and press Accept (or Reject). While an order is still pending you can change a quantity or offer a substitute — the customer must agree before anything changes.
Move it forward as you prepare it, then mark it Ready and Complete. Completing posts the sale and takes the stock.
Cash on delivery: the order is posted as a credit sale; record the money in Payments when you receive it.

online_offers.title: Create an offer or coupon for the online store
online_offers.summary: Dated offers and coupon codes (percent or fixed amount, store-wide or one category).

steps.text: Open Online Store → Offers.

steps: Press New offer, choose percent off or an amount off, the dates, and optionally a coupon code, a category and a minimum order.
Save. Customers see the offer on the shop; the posted sale equals the discounted order total.

qr_menu.summary: A scannable menu or product catalogue for the counter and tables, with optional ordering from the customer's phone.

ledger.does: Records every movement of money as double-entry journal rows.
ledger.proof: Constructor dependency of SaleService and PurchaseService. A sale posts a journal entry.

stock_ledger.does: Records every movement of goods and computes FIFO cost.
stock_ledger.proof: Constructor dependency of SaleService. Every non-service sale deducts stock. Bypassed only when products.type = "service".
stock_ledger.user_words: I always know what I had, and when.

inventory_engine.proof: Called by the stock ledger on every movement.

parties.does: The counterparty record every transaction points at.
parties.proof: parties.type enum [customer, supplier]; ledger rows require party_id.
parties.user_words: Everyone I trade with is remembered.

payments.does: Settles money against documents; multi-account splits; allocation.

tax.proof: Constructor dependency; calculateLineTax() runs on every line.
tax.user_words: Totals are correct without me thinking.

uom.does: Converts every quantity to a base unit before it is stored.
uom.proof: Constructor dependency; toBaseQty() runs on every line.

sequences.does: Numbers every document, gap-free and per-tenant.
sequences.proof: generateTransactionNumber("SAL") on every sale. Duplicate invoice numbers are a legal problem, not a UI problem.
sequences.user_words: My invoices are sequential and legal.

sale.proof: An ERP without transactions is not an ERP.

identity.does: Users, roles, the 49 permission keys, tenant isolation.
identity.proof: Isolation failure is a data breach, not a missing screen.

settlement.does: Closes out balances between parties and accounts.
settlement.proof: Referenced by the money layer; disabling changes balances.

reversal.does: Produces a balanced reversal for any voided document.
reversal.proof: A void that does not reverse the ledger corrupts the books.

audit.does: Immutable record of who changed what.
audit.proof: A switchable audit trail is not an audit trail.

Completing posts the sale and takes the stock. Cash on delivery: the order is posted as a credit sale; record the money in Payments when you receive it.

entries.title: Let staff handle online orders without changing the store settings
entries.text: Let staff handle online orders without changing the store settings. The online store has its own permissions, separate from general settings, so an employee can take orders without being able to change prices, offers, publishing or QR codes. Open Staff and edit the person (or pick the "Online orders clerk" preset when adding them). Under "Online Store & QR Menu" tick only what they need: See Online Orders, Work Online Orders. Leave Online Store Settings, Online Promotions, Choose Online Products and QR Menu & Table Codes unticked. Collecting payment and cancelling an accepted order are separate ticks, so you can keep money actions to trusted people. Vena and Smart Capture access is a separate tick under "Vena & AI"; changing the store's AI key needs "Manage AI Key & Settings".

entries.title: Turn on your online store
entries.text: Turn on your online store. Your online store is a public shop page with a cart and checkout. It needs a short setup, then one Publish click. Make sure the Online Store module is on. Open the System Builder, find "Online Store" and switch it on (it needs the Products module). Open Online Store from the sidebar. Open Settings and fill in: public business name, country and city, address, contact phone, pickup and/or delivery, a payment option that matches (pay at pickup, cash on delivery or bank transfer — bank transfer needs your bank details), and the warehouse that fulfils online orders. Open Products and choose what customers can see: tick products and press Publish. At least one published product is required. Go back to Overview and press "Publish store". If something is missing, the page lists exactly what. Share your store link or QR code from Overview — your first orders land in Orders, where you accept, prepare and complete them.

meta.summary: Your online store is a public shop page with a cart and checkout. It needs a short setup, then one Publish click.

steps.text: Make sure the Online Store module is on. Open the System Builder, find "Online Store" and switch it on (it needs the Products module).

Also called: reservation, reserve stock, booking, advance booking, pre order, block stock, hold stock, presale. Good for: Electronics, appliances, vehicles, anything with a deposit and a wait. Needs: Products, Inventory.

meta.description: Reserve stock against a future sale so it cannot be sold twice.

entries.title: Pricing Tiers & Discounts
entries.text: Pricing Tiers & Discounts. Different prices for different customers — wholesale, retail, staff. Also called: price tier, wholesale price, retail price, discount, rate list, price list, bulk price, thok rate, special price, pricing. Good for: Wholesalers who also sell retail — the most common Pakistani shop shape there is.

meta.description: Different prices for different customers — wholesale, retail, staff.

entries.title: Production Runs
entries.text: Production Runs. Run a batch: consume the ingredients, produce the finished goods. Also called: production, manufacturing, making, baking, assembly, batch production, factory, banana, production run, job work. Good for: Bakeries, food manufacturing, assembly workshops, small factories. Needs: Cookbook / Recipes (BOM).

meta.description: Run a batch: consume the ingredients, produce the finished goods.

entries.title: Products
entries.text: Products. The physical things you sell, with prices and categories. Also called: products, items, catalogue, catalog, goods, stock items, maal, saman, sku, produts. Good for: Every retail, wholesale, food and manufacturing business.

meta.description: The physical things you sell, with prices and categories.

entries.title: Purchase Orders
entries.text: Purchase Orders. Raise an order to a supplier and receive against it, partially or in full. Also called: purchase order, po, indent, requisition, order to supplier, buying order, demand, order book. Good for: Wholesale, distribution, anyone with lead times. Needs: Purchases, Suppliers.

meta.description: Raise an order to a supplier and receive against it, partially or in full.

entries.title: Purchase Returns / Debit Notes
entries.text: Purchase Returns / Debit Notes. Send goods back to a supplier and adjust what you owe them. Also called: purchase return, debit note, return to supplier, supplier return, wapsi, goods return, credit note, debit not. Good for: Any business with a supplier who sometimes ships the wrong thing. Needs: Purchases.

meta.description: Send goods back to a supplier and adjust what you owe them.

entries.title: Purchases
entries.text: Purchases. Record what you buy, what it cost, and what you still owe. Also called: purchase, purchases, buying, procurement, supplier bill, stock in, kharid, khareed, goods received, purchse, inward. Good for: Every business that buys stock rather than making it. Needs: Products.

meta.description: Record what you buy, what it cost, and what you still owe.

entries.title: Quotations
entries.text: Quotations. Send price quotes and turn accepted ones into orders or invoices. Also called: quotation, quote, estimate, proforma, price quote, rate list, offer, quotaion, estimate bill. Good for: Contractors, wholesale, agencies, tender work.

meta.description: Send price quotes and turn accepted ones into orders or invoices.

entries.title: Recurring Invoices
entries.text: Recurring Invoices. Bill the same customer on a schedule without touching it each month. Also called: recurring, subscription, retainer, monthly billing, auto invoice, rent, maheena, standing order, membership billing. Good for: Gyms, rentals, retainers, subscriptions, maintenance contracts. Needs: Invoicing, Customers.

meta.description: Bill the same customer on a schedule without touching it each month.

entries.title: Reports
entries.text: Reports. Every report your system can produce, and none it cannot. Also called: report, reports, reporting, analytics, summary, statement, profit and loss, p&l, balance sheet, sales report, rapot. Good for: Everyone. Auto-scales from a corner shop to a wholesaler.

meta.description: Every report your system can produce, and none it cannot.

entries.title: Sales Orders
entries.text: Sales Orders. Take an order today, fulfil and invoice it later. Also called: sales order, order booking, advance order, custom order, made to order, order, booking, farmaish, pre order. Good for: Made-to-order work: wedding cakes, tailoring, custom furniture, project supply.

meta.description: Take an order today, fulfil and invoice it later.

entries.title: Sales Returns & Refunds
entries.text: Sales Returns & Refunds. Take goods back, refund money or issue credit — correctly, in the books. Also called: return, returns, refund, sales return, credit note, wapsi, wapas, give back, exchange, refunds. Good for: All retail. A shop that cannot take a return is not a shop.

meta.description: Take goods back, refund money or issue credit — correctly, in the books.

entries.title: Serials / IMEI
entries.text: Serials / IMEI. Track individual units by serial or IMEI, from intake to warranty. Also called: serial, serial number, imei, unit tracking, device tracking, warranty tracking, mobile imei, chassis number. Good for: Mobile shops, electronics, appliances, vehicles. Needs: Inventory.

meta.description: Track individual units by serial or IMEI, from intake to warranty.

entries.title: Services
entries.text: Services. The work you do, billed by job, hour or contract — with no stock behind it. Also called: services, jobs, work, labour, labor, repair, appointment, job card, consulting, kaam, mazdoori, servcies. Good for: Freelancers, agencies, salons, consultants, repair shops. THE HIGHEST-VALUE MODULE IN THE PLAN — it is the difference between retail software and business software.

meta.description: The work you do, billed by job, hour or contract — with no stock behind it.

entries.title: Staff & Attendance
entries.text: Staff & Attendance. Who works here, who is on shift, and who did what. Also called: staff, employees, workers, team, attendance, shift, roster, mulazim, hazri, cashiers, timesheet. Good for: Any business with more than one person behind the counter.

meta.description: Who works here, who is on shift, and who did what.

entries.title: Stock Takes & Audit
entries.text: Stock Takes & Audit. Count what is physically there and reconcile it against the books. Also called: stock take, stocktake, physical count, stock count, audit stock, counting, ginti, stock check, cycle count. Good for: Grocery, pharmacy, hardware — anywhere shrinkage is real. Needs: Inventory.

meta.description: Count what is physically there and reconcile it against the books.

entries.title: Stock Transfers
entries.text: Stock Transfers. Move stock between locations with a paper trail on both sides. Also called: transfer, stock transfer, branch transfer, move stock, godown transfer, shift stock, transfer voucher, inter branch. Good for: Anyone with two locations and stock that moves between them. Needs: Inventory, Multi-Location / Warehouses.

meta.description: Move stock between locations with a paper trail on both sides.

entries.title: Suppliers
entries.text: Suppliers. A directory of who you buy from, with balances and statements. Also called: suppliers, vendors, wholesaler, distributor, dealer, party, supplier list, sapplier, buy from. Good for: Anyone who buys stock: retail, grocery, wholesale, restaurants.

meta.description: A directory of who you buy from, with balances and statements.

entries.title: Restaurant & café (FOH)
entries.text: Restaurant & café (FOH). Floor plan, table status and kitchen tickets for dine-in service. Also called: tables, dine in, restaurant, cafe, seating, kot, kitchen order ticket, floor plan, waiter, dhaba, table service. Good for: Restaurants, cafes, dhabas, dine-in of any kind. Needs: POS / Counter, Hold / Park & Recall.

meta.description: Floor plan, table status and kitchen tickets for dine-in service.

entries.title: Tax & Compliance / E-Invoicing
entries.text: Tax & Compliance / E-Invoicing. Tax summaries, rate configuration and government e-invoicing. Also called: tax, gst, vat, sales tax, fbr, e-invoicing, e invoice, compliance, tax return, ntn, filer, withholding. Good for: Registered businesses, anyone filing sales tax, exporters.

meta.description: Tax summaries, rate configuration and government e-invoicing.

entries.title: Units of Measure
entries.text: Units of Measure. Buy in cartons, sell in pieces — conversions handled for you. Also called: unit, units, uom, carton, dozen, kg, litre, piece, packing, bori, conversion, unit conversion. Good for: Grocery, wholesale, agriculture, chemicals, anything sold by weight. Needs: Products.

meta.description: Buy in cartons, sell in pieces — conversions handled for you.

entries.title: Product Variants
entries.text: Product Variants. Size, colour and other variations of the same product. Also called: variant, variants, size color, variations, attributes, options, sizes, colours, colors, nag, style. Good for: Clothing, footwear, hardware, anything sold in sizes. Needs: Products.

entries.title: Audit Events Logged
entries.text: Audit Events Logged Audit Events Logged A safety counter of every action taken in your system, like making a sale, giving a discount, or editing stock. It keeps a record so you always know who did what. Domain: core.

entries.title: Average Transaction Value
entries.text: Average Transaction Value Average Transaction Value The average amount a customer spends when they buy from you. It divides your total sales by the number of customers, showing if people are buying bigger or smaller baskets. Domain: core.

entries.title: Books Balanced
entries.text: Books Balanced Books Balanced A live check that makes sure all your accounts balance. A green mark means every debit matches every credit and there are zero bookkeeping errors in your system. Domain: core.

entries.title: Busiest Day
entries.text: Busiest Day Busiest Day Tells you which day brought in the most sales money. It helps you know which day of the week you need the most staff and the most stock ready. Domain: core.

entries.title: Cash In vs Cash Out
entries.text: Cash In vs Cash Out Cash In vs Cash Out Compares the cash entering your shop against the cash leaving your shop each day. It helps make sure you don't spend more cash on bills than what customers are paying you. Domain: core.

entries.title: Cash in Hand
entries.text: Cash in Hand Cash in Hand The cash you are holding right now: the cash drawer and the safe. Bank money is not counted here. Domain: core.

entries.title: Cost of Goods Sold
entries.text: Cost of Goods Sold Cost of Goods Sold The wholesale cost of the products you actually sold to customers. It only counts items that were sold, so you know exactly how much you paid to buy that inventory from your suppliers. Domain: core.

entries.title: Document Numbering Intact
entries.text: Document Numbering Intact Document Numbering Intact Checks that your invoice and receipt numbers follow in a clean order (like 101, 102, 103) with no missing slips or duplicate numbers. Domain: core.

entries.title: Expense Ratio
entries.text: Expense Ratio Expense Ratio Shows how much of your sales money is eaten up by shop bills. For example, if you sell Rs 100,000 and your shop expenses are Rs 20,000, then 20% of your money goes straight to bills. Domain: core.

entries.title: Total Expenses
entries.text: Total Expenses Total Expenses All the everyday money spent to keep your shop running. This includes shop rent, electricity, staff salaries, internet, tea, repairs, and delivery costs. It does not include buying stock. Domain: core.

entries.title: Gross Margin %
entries.text: Gross Margin % Gross Margin % Shows what percentage of your selling price is profit. For example, a 40% margin means that for every 100 rupees a customer pays you, 40 rupees is profit on the item and 60 rupees covers what you paid to buy it. Domain: core.

entries.title: Gross Profit
entries.text: Gross Profit Gross Profit The profit you make on the items themselves. It takes your sales money and subtracts what you paid to buy those products wholesale. For example, if you sell a shirt for Rs 1,000 that cost you Rs 600, your gross profit is Rs 400. Domain: core.

entries.title: Gross Profit Trend
entries.text: Gross Profit Trend Gross Profit Trend Gross profit (sales minus cost of goods) plotted day by day. Domain: core.

entries.title: Items Sold
entries.text: Items Sold Items Sold How many items (units) you sold in total, across the POS, invoices and online. 50 items at the till plus 50 on invoices is 100 items. Domain: core.

entries.title: Items Sold Trend
entries.text: Items Sold Trend Items Sold Trend Items sold day by day, across every sales channel. Domain: core.

entries.title: Journal Entries Posted
entries.text: Journal Entries Posted Journal Entries Posted The number of accounting records our system created for your shop automatically. Every time you sell, buy, or pay a bill, the system writes the accounting entries for you. Domain: core.

entries.title: Liquidity Trend
entries.text: Liquidity Trend Liquidity Trend A graph tracking your total cash over time. It shows whether your shop is saving more cash day by day or if your bank balance is slowly drying up. Domain: core.

entries.title: Net Cash Position
entries.text: Net Cash Position Net Cash Position The cash you have in hand and bank minus what you owe to suppliers right now. It tells you how much money is truly yours if you paid off all your supplier bills today. Domain: core.

entries.title: Net Margin %
entries.text: Net Margin % Net Margin % Out of every 100 rupees of sales that comes into your shop, this shows how many rupees stay with you as pure profit after paying every single shop bill and expense. Domain: core.

entries.title: Net Profit
entries.text: Net Profit Net Profit The real money you actually take home in your pocket. It takes your sales and subtracts everything: the cost of the products, shop rent, staff wages, electricity bills, tea, and taxes. This is your true final profit. Domain: core.

entries.title: Payables
entries.text: Payables Payables Total money you owe to your suppliers and vendors for stock or services. It shows all the upcoming bills that you need to pay soon. Domain: core.

entries.title: Payables Aging
entries.text: Payables Aging Payables Aging Lists your supplier bills by when they are due. It helps you see which bills need to be paid today and which ones you can pay next week, keeping suppliers happy. Domain: core.

entries.title: Peak Hour
entries.text: Peak Hour Peak Hour The exact hour of the day when the most customers are checking out at your counter. It tells you when you need all cashiers present to handle the rush. Domain: core.

entries.title: Plan Usage
entries.text: Plan Usage Plan Usage Shows how much of your monthly software plan limits you have used, such as number of orders or products. Domain: core.

entries.title: Profit Trend
entries.text: Profit Trend Profit Trend A daily graph showing your actual take-home profit day by day. It shows if you made real money every day or if big bills (like rent or supplier payments) caused you to lose money on certain days. Domain: core.

entries.title: Profit vs Last Period
entries.text: Profit vs Last Period Profit vs Last Period Shows if your real take-home profit grew or shrank compared to last month. It tells you if you are actually keeping more money in your pocket than before. Domain: core.

entries.title: Receivables
entries.text: Receivables Receivables The total money that customers owe you on credit (your customer credit balance). It shows how much of your money is sitting in other people's pockets waiting to be collected. Domain: core.

entries.title: Receivables Aging
entries.text: Receivables Aging Receivables Aging Groups what customers owe you by how late they are (under 30 days, 60 days, or over 90 days). It reminds you which customers to call first before their credit gets too old to collect. Domain: core.

entries.title: Latest Sales
entries.text: Latest Sales Latest Sales The newest completed sales, from every channel. Domain: core.

entries.title: Sales Amount (Revenue)
entries.text: Sales Amount (Revenue) Sales Amount (Revenue) All the money that came into your shop from sales. It adds up every customer payment from your cash register, invoices, and receipts. This is the total money customers handed you before taking out any costs or expenses. Domain: core.

entries.title: Sales Amount Trend
entries.text: Sales Amount Trend Sales Amount Trend A day-by-day graph of your sales. It shows how much money came in each day, so you can easily spot your best sales days, your slow days, and whether your sales are going up or down this month. Domain: core.

entries.title: Revenue vs Last Period
entries.text: Revenue vs Last Period Revenue vs Last Period Shows if your sales are higher or lower compared to last month or last week. A green number means more customers are buying from you than before. Domain: core.

entries.title: Reversals & Corrections
entries.text: Reversals & Corrections Reversals & Corrections Counts how many times a sale or bill was cancelled, returned, or corrected. A high number helps you catch cashier mistakes or customer return issues early. Domain: core.

entries.title: Sales by Category
entries.text: Sales by Category Sales by Category What you sold, split by product category. Shows which categories bring in the most money. Domain: core.

entries.title: Sales of One Category
entries.text: Sales of One Category Sales of One Category What you sold in the one product category you pick. Choose the category in the Data step. Domain: core.

entries.title: Sales of One Category Trend
entries.text: Sales of One Category Trend Sales of One Category Trend Sales of the one category you pick, day by day. Choose the category in the Data step. Domain: core.

entries.title: Number of Sales
entries.text: Number of Sales Number of Sales How many separate sales you made (POS and invoices together). Revenue is the money; this is the count. Domain: core.

entries.title: Sales Count Trend
entries.text: Sales Count Trend Sales Count Trend Number of sales plotted day by day, so you can see your busy and quiet days. Domain: core.

entries.title: Total Balance
entries.text: Total Balance Total Balance All the ready cash you have right now. It adds up all the cash inside your cash drawer and safe, plus all the money in every bank account you have. Domain: core.

entries.title: Transactions
entries.text: Transactions Transactions The total number of customer sales and printed receipts. It tells you how busy your checkout counter was, counting every visit whether the customer spent Rs 50 or Rs 50,000. Domain: core.

entries.title: Active Users
entries.text: Active Users Active Users Shows which of your staff members and cashiers have logged into the system and are working today. Domain: core.

entries.title: Working Capital
entries.text: Working Capital Working Capital Your financial breathing room. It checks if your current stock, cash, and customer dues are enough to easily cover your short-term bills and keep your shop running smoothly. Domain: core.

entries.title: Active Customers
entries.text: Active Customers Active Customers Customers who actually bought something in the period. Domain: customers.

entries.title: Average Customer Spend
entries.text: Average Customer Spend Average Customer Spend What a typical customer is worth in the period. Domain: customers.

entries.title: Customers by Area
entries.text: Customers by Area Customers by Area Where your customers are, so you know which area actually pays. Domain: customers.

entries.title: Total Customers
entries.text: Total Customers Total Customers Every customer on your books. Domain: customers.

entries.title: Dormant Customers
entries.text: Dormant Customers Dormant Customers Regulars who have gone quiet — the cheapest sales list you own. Domain: customers.

entries.title: New Customers
entries.text: New Customers New Customers People who bought from you for the first time in the period. Domain: customers.

entries.title: New Customer Trend
entries.text: New Customer Trend New Customer Trend First-time buyers plotted across the period. Domain: customers.

entries.title: Customers Who Owe You
